subject: FastRetail POC: evaluation playbook and observability runway
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Green <oliver.green@fastretail.com>, Diana Mendez <diana.mendez@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Feb 2026 23:10:00 +0000
Subject: Recap from today — POC scope and observability runway

Oliver / Diana — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared playbook heading into the trial kickoff.

TL;DR — FastRetail trial (4 weeks) -> success criteria that validate inference quality + cost/latency at your peak traffic pattern -> observability to measure those signals end-to-end.

Proposed POC scope and milestones:
- Week 0 (prep): network allowlist, sample traffic, and test prompts submitted by FastRetail.
- Week 1: baseline runs on Redwood hosted instance; dashboard + traces live; sample evals executed.
- Week 2–3: ramp synthetic+real traffic; run mutation/edge-case prompts; collect cost/throughput metrics.
- Week 4: handoff report + recommendations (quantization, batching, model variant).

Initial success criteria (please confirm / adjust):
1) Latency: 95th percentile end-to-end inference < 600ms for 75-token prompts at expected concurrency.
2) Quality: >= 92% pass rate on your curated prompt set (accuracy/relevance thresholds you provide).
3) Economics: token cost parity within 20% of your budget target (we'll model after we get traffic profile).
4) Reliability: <0.5% error rate and graceful fallback to smaller model if capacity constrained.

Observability items we need live for the POC:
- Per-request tracing with request-id and span for routing/queueing/inference kernels.
- Dashboards: p50/p95/p99 latency, token throughput (tokens/sec), batch size distribution, KV cache hit rate, model-fallback counts, and error rates by type.
- Logs exported to your S3 (or secure bucket) with a prefix for the POC; include structured fields (request_id, model_name, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, error_code).
- Cost telemetry: tokens consumed per route and per model variant.

Action items for FastRetail (please confirm owners and ETA):
- Provide sample workload (JSON) + 20–30 seed prompts — owner: Oliver? ETA: Feb 6
- Network allowlist details for Redwood endpoints — owner: Diana? ETA: Feb 5

Internal ask (Redwood):
- Assign owners for dashboards, tracing, log export, and eval harness.
- Draft kickoff agenda and send calendar invite.

Attaching: FastRetail_MVP_eval_template.xlsx (template for your prompt sets and scoring rubric).

If this matches your expectations, propose we kick off week of Feb 9 and schedule a 60-min technical kickoff.

Thanks —
Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Oliver Green <oliver.green@fastretail.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Diana Mendez <diana.mendez@fastretail.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Feb 2026 09:18:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Recap from today — POC scope and observability runway

Priyom — thanks for the clear recap. This aligns with our view. A few quick notes / clarifications from our side:

- We can commit to a 4-week trial starting Feb 9.
- Success criteria: tweak on quality — we'll provide an acceptance rubric where a prompt is "pass" if top-3 outputs contain a correct SKU or matching product title. Expect ~300 prompts across categories.
- Security: our InfoSec requires that audit logs for admin actions be retained for 90 days; we'll share the list of fields they need.

Owners on our side:
- Sample prompts + rubric: Oliver Green (I'll attach the sheet by Feb 6).
- Network / firewall: Diana Mendez — attaching current ACL config for your infra team.

We are fine with logs exported to an S3 bucket (we'll create a dedicated bucket and share credentials).

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.

Oliver Green
Head of Platforms | FastRetail
oliver.green@fastretail.com
Attachment: FR_network_acl.pdf

Subject: Internal — FastRetail POC tasks, owners, and observability deliverables

Team — forwarding the FastRetail confirmation. They want a Feb 9 kickoff and will provide the prompts and ACLs. Please see proposed owner breakdown and deadlines below.

Tech tasks (owners / target dates):
- Dashboard build (Grafana/Redwood Console views): owner: Neha Kapoor — target: Feb 7 (initial), Feb 12 (validated).
  - Panels: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, batch-size histogram, cache hit rate, model fallback counter, errors by category.
- Tracing instrumentation + sampling policy: owner: Neha Kapoor — target: Feb 8. Ensure request-id propagation and spans for routing -> queue -> kernel.
- Log export pipeline (structured JSON -> S3 prefix s3://fastretail-poc/2026-02/): owner: Marissa Cole — target: Feb 7 (pipeline in place), Feb 9 (first exports).
- Eval harness + scoring (runners and scripts for their rubric): owner: Ben Carter — target: Feb 11 (first pass).
- Cost model runbook: owner: Priyom Das — target: Feb 12. Provide token-cost per route and candidate optimizations (batching, quantization trade-offs).

Operational checks: quota limits, canary routing policy, and automatic fallback to smaller model variant in case of quota pressure. Ben — please validate we have a canary and rollback policy defined in the trial config.

Marissa — please prep the kickoff-agenda.odt and include an itemized ask list for FastRetail (sample traffic format, S3 creds, expected concurrency).

Related artifacts: redwood_poc_checklist.md (I attached a working draft).

Let me know if any dates are tight. We should confirm the Feb 9 kickoff invite by EOD Feb 5.

—Priyom

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 5 Feb 2026 11:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Internal — FastRetail POC tasks, owners, and observability deliverables

Acknowledged — I'll own dashboards and tracing. A few implementation notes from my side:

Metrics and panels I'll publish:
- Latency: p50/p75/p90/p95/p99 (server-side + end-to-end), include distribution heatmap.
- Throughput: tokens/sec and requests/sec, split by client route.
- Batch characteristics: average vs max batch size, distribution.
- Cache: KV cache hit rate and miss reasons.
- Model variants: count of requests served by primary vs fallback variant (important for SLA).
- Errors: 4xx/5xx by subtype and correlation with model exception messages.
- Cost telemetry: tokens per request and estimated $/1k-tokens (we can approximate until finance provides exact rates).

Tracing plan:
- We'll instrument spans at the gateway, routing, batching, and kernel-exec points. Each trace will include request_id, client_route, model_variant, and token counts.
- Sampling: full traces for 1% of requests, 100% tracing for requests that hit error codes or model fallbacks.

Data export notes:
- For S3 export, we'll use newline-delimited JSON with these fields: ts, request_id, model, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, batch_size, error_code. Marissa — confirm you have write IAM details for the bucket.

Tight timeline but feasible — I'll push the dashboard skeleton by Feb 7 and wire in live metrics by Feb 8. Need the sample traffic by Feb 6 to tune filters and sampling.

-Neha
Lead Observability Engineer | Redwood Inference
